OULAD — model¶

This notebook asks whether risk changes with the course context and whether that context carries into a student-level prediction. Calculations come from functions in the data_science package. The model, the metrics, and the charts are not written here.

Question¶

Does risk change with the course context? Does course context carry into a student-level prediction? Are the same features used for a course never seen in training?

Design¶

The feature sets are as follows.

GENERAL carries assessment and virtual-learning activity up to the cutoff day, plus the registration day. Click counts by activity type are included. The module code and earlier presentations are absent.

GENERAL_MODULE adds the module code to those columns.

HISTORY adds the earlier presentations' module risk rate, slot score, slot submission rate, the score gap from the historical slot, and an indicator that history exists.

HISTORY_SLOT adds the slot score, the slot submission rate, the score gap from the historical slot, and the history indicator. The module risk rate is not in this set.

GENERAL_REL replaces raw values with percentile ranks inside the same module presentation. The ranks cover score, submission ratio, clicks, active days, recency of the last activity, and delay. The registration day stays beside them. The module code is absent. The risk label is not read when the ranks are computed.

The model types are logreg and hgb.

Tuning fits on the first presentation in the train split. Selection uses log loss on the next presentation. The chosen settings are refit on the whole train split. The test presentation is evaluated once, at the end. Intervals come from bootstrap samples stratified by class inside each module.

HISTORY_SLOT and GENERAL_REL were added after the first test results were seen. Both are exploratory. The test split stays frozen, and the validation period is reported on its own.

The cell prints the presentations, the columns in each set, and the chosen settings.

from pathlib import Path
import base64
import html
import json
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

ROOT = Path.cwd().resolve()
if not (ROOT / "data_science").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from data_science.oulad import PROCESSED_OULAD_DIR
from data_science.oulad.dataset import FEATURES_NAME
from data_science.oulad.explain import build_report
from data_science.oulad.figures import write_figures
from data_science.oulad.model import (
    FIT_PRESENTATION,
    MODEL_NAMES,
    SET_NAMES,
    TEST_PRESENTATION,
    VAL_PRESENTATION,
    compare_models,
    feature_columns,
)
from data_science.oulad.relative import add_relative_features
from data_science.oulad.rule import compare_rule

LANG = "en"


def dump_json(path, payload):
    def convert(value):
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return {str(key): convert(item) for key, item in value.items()}
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
            return [convert(item) for item in value]
        if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
            return convert(value.tolist())
        if isinstance(value, np.floating):
            value = float(value)
        if isinstance(value, float):
            if np.isnan(value):
                return None
            return float(value)
        if isinstance(value, (np.integer, int)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
            return int(value)
        return value

    Path(path).write_text(
        json.dumps(convert(payload), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


def format_estimate(value):
    return f"{float(value):.6f}"


def format_interval(item):
    return (
        f"{format_estimate(item['estimate'])} "
        f"[{format_estimate(item['low'])}, {format_estimate(item['high'])}]"
    )


def show_table(frame):
    missing = [column for column in ("n", "n_positive") if column not in frame.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(missing)
    print(
        frame.to_string(
            index=False,
            max_colwidth=None,
            float_format=lambda value: f"{float(value):.6f}",
        )
    )


def show_figure(stem):
    spec = next(item for item in catalog if item["dosya"] == stem)
    alt = spec[f"alt_{LANG}"]
    encoded = base64.b64encode((FIG_DIR / f"{stem}_{LANG}.png").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
    display(
        HTML(
            f'<img alt="{html.escape(alt, quote=True)}" '
            f'src="data:image/png;base64,{encoded}">'
        )
    )
    display(Markdown(alt))


frame = pd.read_parquet(PROCESSED_OULAD_DIR / FEATURES_NAME, engine="pyarrow")
report, _predictions = compare_models(frame)
del _predictions
params = dict(report["selected_params"]["GENERAL"]["hgb"]["params"])
explain = build_report(frame, params)
rule_report = compare_rule(frame, params)

FIG_DIR = ROOT / "notebooks" / f"_figtmp_{LANG}"
FIG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for child in FIG_DIR.iterdir():
    if child.is_file():
        child.unlink()
dump_json(FIG_DIR / "model_metrics.json", report)
dump_json(FIG_DIR / "explain.json", explain)
write_figures(FIG_DIR / "model_metrics.json", FIG_DIR / "explain.json", FIG_DIR)
catalog = json.loads((FIG_DIR / "figures.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

TEST_N = int(sum(row["n"] for row in report["modules"]["rows"]))
TEST_N_POSITIVE = int(sum(row["n_positive"] for row in report["modules"]["rows"]))
_validation_modules = [
    row for row in report["validation"]["modules"]["rows"] if row["set"] == "GENERAL"
]
VAL_N = int(sum(row["n"] for row in _validation_modules))
VAL_N_POSITIVE = int(sum(row["n_positive"] for row in _validation_modules))
SELECTED = report["modules"]["model"]

rows = []
for presentation, part in frame.groupby(frame["code_presentation"].astype(str), sort=True):
    splits = part["split"].astype(str).unique()
    if len(splits) != 1:
        raise ValueError(presentation)
    rows.append(
        {
            "code_presentation": str(presentation),
            "split": str(splits[0]),
            "n": int(len(part)),
            "n_positive": int((part["at_risk"] == 1).sum()),
        }
    )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))
print(f"fit_presentation={FIT_PRESENTATION}")
print(f"validation_presentation={VAL_PRESENTATION}")
print(f"test_presentation={TEST_PRESENTATION}")

described = add_relative_features(frame)
rows = []
sample_n = int(len(described))
sample_positive = int((described["at_risk"] == 1).sum())
for set_name in SET_NAMES:
    for column in feature_columns(set_name, list(described.columns)):
        rows.append(
            {
                "set": set_name,
                "column": column,
                "n": sample_n,
                "n_positive": sample_positive,
            }
        )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))

rows = []
for set_name in SET_NAMES:
    for model_name in MODEL_NAMES:
        chosen = report["selected_params"][set_name][model_name]
        chosen_params = chosen["params"]
        rows.append(
            {
                "set": set_name,
                "model": model_name,
                "scope": "validation",
                "n": VAL_N,
                "n_positive": VAL_N_POSITIVE,
                "val_log_loss": chosen["val_log_loss"],
                "params": ",".join(f"{key}={chosen_params[key]}" for key in chosen_params),
            }
        )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))

The cell prints test metrics and paired differences. A paired difference subtracts the right set from the left set on the same bootstrap samples.

Two periods¶

The chart joins validation and test ROC AUC for the sets. The table places the same values side by side. The set with the highest test ROC AUC sits lower on validation.

rows = []
for set_name in SET_NAMES:
    validation = next(
        row["roc_auc"]
        for row in report["validation"]["rows"]
        if row["set"] == set_name and row["model"] == "hgb"
    )
    test = report["test_metrics"][set_name]["hgb"]["roc_auc"]
    rows.append(
        {
            "set": set_name,
            "model": "hgb",
            "n": TEST_N,
            "n_positive": TEST_N_POSITIVE,
            "validation_n": VAL_N,
            "validation_n_positive": VAL_N_POSITIVE,
            "validation_roc_auc": validation,
            "test_roc_auc": test["estimate"],
            "test_roc_auc_low": test["low"],
            "test_roc_auc_high": test["high"],
        }
    )
table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
table = table.sort_values(["test_roc_auc", "set"], ascending=[False, True], kind="mergesort")
show_table(table.reset_index(drop=True))

Each line joins validation and test ROC AUC for one feature set. The thick lines are the general and relative general sets; the others are thin. Only the test point has a ninety-five percent interval. The validation point has no interval.

Base-rate shift¶

The chart shows the actual rate and the mean prediction by module in the test period. The tables place the historical module rate beside the rate in that period and print how many distinct hist_module_risk_rate values appear in the train split. Within-module ROC AUC is a separate table.

In [5]:
show_figure("fig02_oran_kaymasi")

train = frame.loc[frame["split"].astype(str).eq("train")]
test = frame.loc[frame["split"].astype(str).eq("test")]
hist_train = pd.to_numeric(train["hist_module_risk_rate"], errors="coerce")
show_table(
    pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "split": "train",
                "n": int(len(train)),
                "n_positive": int((train["at_risk"] == 1).sum()),
                "n_distinct_hist_module_risk_rate": int(hist_train.nunique(dropna=True)),
            }
        ]
    )
)

train_module = train["code_module"].astype(str)
test_module = test["code_module"].astype(str)
train_distinct = hist_train.groupby(train_module).nunique(dropna=True)
train_n = train.groupby(train_module).size()
train_positive = train.groupby(train_module)["at_risk"].sum()
rows = []
for name, part in test.groupby(test_module, sort=True):
    hist = pd.to_numeric(part["hist_module_risk_rate"], errors="coerce")
    distinct = int(hist.nunique(dropna=True))
    observed = hist.dropna()
    rows.append(
        {
            "code_module": str(name),
            "n": int(len(part)),
            "n_positive": int((part["at_risk"] == 1).sum()),
            "hist_module_risk_rate": float(observed.iloc[0]) if distinct == 1 else float("nan"),
            "positive_rate": float(part["at_risk"].mean()),
            "test_n_distinct_hist_module_risk_rate": distinct,
            "train_n": int(train_n.get(name, 0)),
            "train_n_positive": int(train_positive.get(name, 0)),
            "train_n_distinct_hist_module_risk_rate": int(train_distinct.get(name, 0)),
        }
    )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))

rows = []
for row in report["modules"]["rows"]:
    flat = {
        "model": report["modules"]["model"],
        "code_module": row["code_module"],
        "n": row["n"],
        "n_positive": row["n_positive"],
    }
    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
        value = row["roc_auc"][set_name]
        flat[set_name] = float("nan") if value is None else value
    rows.append(flat)

Unseen course¶

The chart shows the mean prediction and the actual rate for a course never seen in training. LOMO drops each module from training without retuning the chosen hgb settings and evaluates that module on the test presentation. The last tables count expected assessments and observed scores up to the cutoff day. GGG rows have no expected assessment and no observed score.

What the model relies on¶

The chart uses SHAP to show which columns the general hgb model relies on. Positive SHAP is the direction in which the model increases predicted risk. That direction is not a cause.

        {
            "set": shap["set"],

            "feature": item["feature"],
            "mean_abs_shap": item["mean_abs_shap"],
            "n": TEST_N,
            "n_positive": TEST_N_POSITIVE,
            "n_explained": int(shap["n_explained"]),
        }
    )
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows))

Bridge to the school system¶

The school system has no training label. The transparent rule does not use one. It is the mean of the within-presentation ranks for unsubmitted assessments, score, and active days. The rule and the general hgb model sit side by side on the same eligible students in the validation and test presentations. The cost in precision is visible in this table.

Limitations¶

The data come from one institution. Fail and Withdrawn are the same class. LOMO rows have no interval. There is a single validation period. The test split was seen more than once; that use is evaluation only and does not retune the settings. SHAP is not a cause.

OZET¶

The cell prints the summary as key=value lines.
